rows: Geothermal gradient averages 25–30°C per km in the crust; powered by radioactive decay and residual heat
Increases steadily with depth alongside temperature

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Both temperature and pressure increase consistently with increasing depth.
The average geothermal gradient within the Earth's crust is 25–30°C per kilometer.
Earth's internal heat originates from two main sources: radioactive decay and residual heat from its formation.
The exact range of the crustal geothermal gradient (25–30°C per km) is a frequently asked factual question in geography papers.
Identify radioactive decay and residual heat from formation as the twin heat sources of Earth's interior.
Remember that BOTH temperature and pressure increase with depth; do not confuse crustal trends with atmospheric layers.
